subject: Qualification recap + request: custom eval playbook and dataset from Catalyst Health
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Emily Bullard <emily.bullard@catalysthealth.com>, Jared Lopez <jared.lopez@catalysthealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 05 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Qualification recap + request: custom eval playbook and dataset from Catalyst Health

Hi Emily & Jared,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — excellent conversation. Quick recap and clear next steps so we can scope a focused model-fit eval on Redwood and give you a cost/latency estimate for the pilot: 

Recap (short):
- Primary goal: automate triage and routing suggestions for inbound referral notes with high precision on diagnosis extraction and intent (3 top slots + confidence).
- Quality target: reduce manual triage time by 30% and achieve >=85% top-3 accuracy on our benchmark prompts.
- Data constraints: PHI will remain in your environment; we will run the customer-specific eval on Redwood Private (VPC) — you requested a non-hosted setup.

Requested from Catalyst to start the eval on our side: (1) small gold dataset (200–500 rows) in the template attached, (2) canonical label schema and edge-case notes, (3) indication of any redaction rules or PII masking you want retained.

Redwood recommendations for initial model candidates (based on your latency & accuracy tradeoff ask):
- rdx-chat-7b-v2 (int8 quant) — low-latency candidate for live routing, expected median token latency <40ms on Dedicated capacity.
- rdx-chat-13b-q4f16 — stronger accuracy with modest latency increase; good for batched evaluation runs.
- rdx-chat-70b-mml (float16) — highest quality for semantic extraction; recommend only for scoring and manual adjudication passes due to cost.

Evaluation plan outline (we can run this inside your VPC):
1) Ingest: you upload CSV (sample attached) to a secure S3 bucket we provision. Template: id,input_text,reference_labels,metadata (json string).
2) Prompt bank: we’ll use the attached prompt set + your edge-case examples; please mark any prompts that must be redacted.
3) Metrics: top-3 exact match, normalized entity F1, and embedding-based semantic similarity (embedding cosine >=0.84 considered acceptable).
4) Human review: anything below confidence 0.6 is queued for adjudication. We’ll provide an adjudication UI link for your reviewers.
5) Deliverables: evaluation report (accuracy/latency/cost), example failure cases, scorer notebook, and recommended rollout config for Dedicated/Private.

Next steps (actionable):
- Emily: upload the 200–500 sample CSV to the Drive link I shared OR drop in the attached sample to this thread by EOD Monday.
- Ben & Priyom: please confirm scoring thresholds and if we should include BLEU/BLEURT as secondary metrics or stick to entity F1 + embedding sim.
- Redwood will provide a proposed workback and cost estimate within 48 hours after sample receipt.

Attachments: redwood-eval-template.jsonl, catalyst_eval_samples.csv (sample redacted), SLA-digest.pdf

Thanks,

Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com | (415) 555-0198

From: Emily Bullard <emily.bullard@catalysthealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 05 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Qualification recap + request: custom eval playbook and dataset from Catalyst Health

Thanks Vanessa — this is helpful and aligned with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Data: we will provide a 300-row gold set (de-identified) with the schema you listed. The metadata column will include: source_system, note_type, created_at, provider_id.
2) Labels: for the label column we will provide a JSON array of target entities (diagnosis_code, intent_tag, routing_team). Example in the sample CSV.
3) Redaction: please do not retain original patient names; we will deliver already de-identified. Full PHI will remain on our S3; we expect Redwood to run the eval inside our VPC and never export the raw text.
4) Metrics: we are most interested in entity F1 and top-3 routing accuracy. We like the embedding similarity idea for fuzzy matching — set threshold at 0.8 on the first pass.

Two asks: can you confirm the exact evaluation runtime estimate for the 300-row run with the three model candidates? Also, include recommended batch-size and expected cost per model candidate so we can budget.

We’ll upload the file to the Drive link by EOD Monday.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Emily
Emily Bullard
Head of Data Science | Catalyst Health
emily.bullard@catalysthealth.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Emily Bullard <emily.bullard@catalysthealth.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 06 May 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Qualification recap + request: custom eval playbook and dataset from Catalyst Health

Hi Emily — looping on scoring details. A couple of clarifications from Redwood ops that will affect runtime/cost:

- For a 300-row dataset and the three model candidates, approximate single-run inference time estimates inside Dedicated/Private (ballpark, assuming standard seq length ~220 tokens):
  * rdx-chat-7b-v2 (int8): ~6–8 minutes, recommended batch_size=16.
  * rdx-chat-13b-q4f16: ~12–16 minutes, recommended batch_size=8.
  * rdx-chat-70b-mml (fp16): ~40–55 minutes, batch_size=4 (GPU memory permitting).

- Cost estimate per model (compute only, rounding): rdx-7b: ~$12; rdx-13b: ~$38; rdx-70b: ~$210. These assume no heavy human adjudication time.

Scoring thresholds suggestion:
- top-3 accuracy target: >=0.85 to mark as acceptable for routing; anything between 0.7–0.85 flagged for manual review.
- entity F1: target >=0.82.
- embedding cosine: keep at 0.8 as Emily suggested; we’ll run a small calibration pass and report distribution.

Priyom — can you take point on the eval job setup? I’ve attached a short checklist: convert CSV -> JSONL (one record per line with id,input,labels,meta), upload to the S3 path Vanessa will provision, create eval job with the three model pins, and set output storage to your supplied bucket (no data exported to Redwood-hosted buckets).

I’ll draft the quick workback and estimate once we have the actual sample.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Emily Bullard <emily.bullard@catalysthealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 06 May 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Qualification recap + request: custom eval playbook and dataset from Catalyst Health

Perfect — thanks everyone. Emily, once you upload the file I’ll start the provisioning (S3 role + KMS key config) and Priyom will kick off the conversion pipeline and a dry-run to validate the JSONL. Expect our official workback and cost callout within 48 hours of receipt.

Quick notes for the file upload (to avoid friction):
- Use the attached CSV template; ensure the metadata column is valid JSON with double quotes.
- If you have nested lists in labels, flatten them into arrays in the reference_labels field (we’ll show an example in the template).
- For adjudication sampling, mark 25 random rows with "priority_review=true" in metadata so our human-review UI will surface them first.

Ben/Priyom: once the dry-run completes, please send the eval-job link and the preliminary runtime log to hubspot and the Drive folder. I’ll follow up with a short internal exec note for our leadership team summarizing risk and expected SLA alignment.

Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com | (415) 555-0198
